title: National Hairston Clan v. Stokes County: Community Groups File Second Suit to Void 1,850-Acre Project Delta Data Center Rezoning
jurisdiction: North Carolina Superior Court, Stokes County
amount: Order voiding the rezoning and injunctive relief
summary: On November 12, 2026, four community organizations and a group of residents filed a new suit in Stokes County Superior Court challenging the Board of Commissioners' 3-2 vote on September 14 to rezone about 1,850 acres along the Dan River near Walnut Cove for a hyperscale data center campus known as Project Delta. The plaintiffs say the approval rested on a rushed analysis that appears to have been AI-generated and was never independently checked, and that it conflicts with the county's long-range plan. They ask the court to void the rezoning and bar the county from relying on it. An earlier rezoning of the same land was voided by consent judgment in August after the same lawyers sued over notice defects.
significance: The suit shows that curing a notice defect and re-voting does not end the litigation risk on a large rezoning; the second round attacks the quality of the county's analysis itself. It also puts a pending 15-year development agreement in play, which the plaintiffs say would exempt the site from any future data center moratorium and commit the county to help defend the developer. For data center developers, landowners and capital sources, the case is a reminder that entitlement on a speculative, no-named-user site remains contestable long after the vote.
